# vantorr

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

The `vantorr` package provides an R interface to the [Maxar / Vantor Hub APIs](https://developers.maxar.com/docs/), enabling programmatic access to high-resolution satellite imagery (such as Vivid Mosaic basemaps, WorldView archives, and analysis-ready data). It natively integrates with `sf`, `terra`, and `stars`.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `vantorr` from [GitHub](https://github.com/michael-cw/vantorr) with:

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("michael-cw/vantorr")
```

## Authentication

The Vantor API supports both **API Keys** (long-lived, up to 180 days) and **OAuth 2.0 Bearer Tokens** (session-based, with automatic refresh).

You can configure credentials in your `.Renviron` file (`VANTOR_API_KEY`, or `VANTOR_USERNAME` and `VANTOR_PASSWORD`) or set them interactively for your R session with `vantor_auth()`:

```{r auth_example}
library(vantorr)

# Option 1: Set an API Key for the session
vantor_auth(api_key = "your_api_key")

# Option 2: Authenticate via OAuth2 (automatically caches and refreshes tokens)
vantor_auth(username = "your_email@example.com", password = "your_password")
```

## Usage

`vantorr` accepts spatial objects from `sf`, `terra`, and `stars` (as well as numeric bounding boxes in `EPSG:4326` or `EPSG:3857`) and automatically transforms coordinates to the required projection.

```{r usage_example}
library(vantorr)
library(sf)
library(terra)

# Define an Area of Interest (AOI) in WGS84 (EPSG:4326)
aoi <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -77.040, ymin = 38.888, xmax = -77.030, ymax = 38.892),
  crs = st_crs(4326)
)

# Retrieve a 30cm Vivid Basemap directly as a terra SpatRaster
basemap_rast <- get_maxar_wms_basemap(
  bbox = aoi,
  resolution = 0.3,
  product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30",
  return_type = "SpatRaster"
)

terra::plotRGB(basemap_rast, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3, stretch = "lin")
```

For larger areas of interest that exceed single-request pixel limits, use `get_maxar_wms_tiles()` to automatically grid, download, and mosaic tiles:

```{r tiles_example}
large_mosaic <- get_maxar_wms_tiles(
  bbox = aoi,
  tile_size = 2500,
  resolution = 0.3,
  merge_tiles = TRUE,
  return_type = "SpatRaster"
)
```
